source_review.notes: Checked all eight structured references at AWS, Google Cloud, dbt Labs, Apache Beam, PostgreSQL, Snowflake, and OpenLineage; each returned HTTP 200, with the dbt terms URL resolving to its maintained ELT article. Claims about ETL/ELT ordering, Beam pipeline constructs, PostgreSQL COPY append behavior, BigQuery loading interfaces, Snowflake DDL transaction behavior, and lineage object types match the cited sources and remain product/version/boundary scoped.

evidence: Checked source population I_c, extraction E, pre-target transform T_s, raw target load L_r, target transform T_t, curated load L_c, ETL/ELT outputs, input/output manifests, transformation version, trusted pointer, stage rates, and lifecycle cost for stable meanings.
Draft chapter validation accepted every required heading and all GitHub-compatible inline and display-math delimiters.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Extraction, physical load, semantic transform, trusted publication, raw recovery, and output generation remain separate functions and boundaries.

evidence: Executed the annotated Decimal fixture: three source records yield two ETL and two lossless-ELT rows; both total 3,006 cents; lossy half-even pre-coercion yields 3,005 cents; one record is filtered; original/lossless replay is stable.
Recomputed Exercise 2: half-away values are 10.01, -10.01, and 20.05; half-even pre-coercion yields 10.00, -10.00, and 20.05; both totals happen to equal 20.05 while two row values differ.
Checked the batch-latency sum and bottleneck-throughput expressions dimensionally: time terms add only for non-overlapped stages, and minimum stage rate bounds safe steady-state throughput.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All explicit source/row/filter counts and cent/decimal results reproduce, including the total-equality counterexample to row-level equivalence.

evidence: Verified ETL composition L_c(T_s(E(I_c))) and ELT composition T_t(L_r(E(I_c))) are not generally commutative because load may coerce, filter, default, constrain, reorder, or create side effects.
Verified conditional equivalence requires equality for every permitted I_c under the declared row/type/order/side-effect/publication relation, not one sampled dataset.
Verified that if lossy L_r maps distinct required inputs x and y to one representation, no deterministic downstream T_t can distinguish them and reproduce a T_s that maps them differently.
Verified cost decomposition is an accounting model and throughput/latency formulae are capacity approximations, not semantic results.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The algebra makes transformation placement, information loss, publication, capacity, and cost claims independently reviewable.

Reviewed sensitive raw, minimization/tokenization, tenant/residency/egress, source and target contention, skew/scale, cost, lineage gaps, disaster recovery, artifact/dependency drift, and current-versus-original recomputation.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The ten examples and five exercises span ETL, ELT, hybrid, security, types, bulk loading, transactions, incremental flow, equivalence, cost, and recovery.

Checked load append/replace/merge/snapshot semantics, generation-specific staging, exact manifest membership, quality gates, target receipt, and conditional/atomic publication.

invariant_checking.notes: The invariants preserve semantic and operational contracts regardless of which engine executes a transform.

evidence: Reviewed the conditional placement-equivalence proof from identical I_c through lossless-enough raw load, equivalent target transform, equivalent curated load/publication, and deterministic/idempotent execution.
Checked each premise can fail independently through lossy coercion, different source/reference cuts, engine type/null/time/order semantics, error policy, transaction behavior, or external effects.
Reviewed the information-loss argument as a counterexample schema: L_r(x)=L_r(y) with T_s(x) unequal to T_s(y) makes any deterministic T_t after L_r unable to preserve both results.
Reviewed output comparison as a declared equivalence relation rather than assumed byte identity or equal count.
proof_review.notes: The theorem does not favor ETL or ELT; it identifies sufficient equivalence premises and makes loss or changed semantics explicit.

evidence: The placement-equivalence result is labeled conditional and lists source, fidelity, transform-semantic, load/publication, determinism, and idempotence premises immediately before its proof.
Named-target, source-cut, raw-fidelity, type-order, load, publication, incremental, dependency, security, quality-lineage, and cost/evidence claims are labeled invariants or boundaries.
AWS/Google/dbt terminology and Beam, PostgreSQL, BigQuery, Snowflake, and OpenLineage behavior are source-attributed rather than generalized across engines.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Deduction, vendor terminology, product contract, operational recommendation, capacity estimate, and finite example remain distinguishable.

evidence: The executable fixture explicitly limits itself to one three-row Decimal example and disclaims general equivalence, database semantics, distributed execution, security, transactions, cost, and publication.
Benchmark/cost evidence is scoped to measured volume, skew, concurrency, configuration, prices, failures, and recovery horizon and is not used to infer semantic equivalence.
Equal row counts/totals, successful loader commands, raw-load freshness, green orchestration, same code labels, and parsed lineage are each assigned explicit evidence limits.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Production placement decisions require deployed semantic comparisons, resource/cost measurements, failure injection, security approval, and recovery evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed distinctions among named target and landing store; acquisition and business transform; physical load and trusted publication; staging and output; ETL, ELT, and hybrid; source pushdown and target transform; append, replace, merge, and snapshot; source cut and ingestion time; reproduction and recomputation; equivalent count and equivalent semantics.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable placement matrices, source extraction/raw capture, staging/manifests, target bulk loads and transaction semantics, type/null/time/reference behavior, full/incremental/delete flows, quality gates, idempotent retries, schema evolution, control-plane states, artifact versioning, lineage, latency/throughput/cost models, security, hybrid design, semantic comparison, and failure/DR tests.

pedagogical_review.notes: The one-page review replaces slogan comparisons with composition and placement; exposition progresses through source/load/transform semantics, target/external execution, types, security, batch/incremental operations, control, lineage, capacity, and hybrid selection; the runnable counterexample demonstrates non-commutativity; and ten examples plus five solved exercises require architectural judgment.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. References and local execution were checked on 2026-09-02. The finite model and documentation review do not establish any deployed source cut, load fidelity, database transaction/DDL semantics, transformation equivalence, raw replayability, target publication, security/privacy compliance, schema evolution, resource capacity, pricing/cost, lineage completeness, idempotence, or disaster recovery; those require system-specific contracts and production evidence.
